newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean navy ships confront N.Korean vessels.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean navy ships confront N.Korean vessels.

text.p: South Korean navy vessels briefly confronted North Korean patrol boats on Thursday but the Northern ships withdrew without any incident, a South Korean military spokesman said.
"The North Korean boats entered the southern water briefly this morning to stop a Chinese fishing boat heading south in the Yellow Sea," he said.
"Our navy vessels were immediately dispatched but the northern ships and the fishing boat returned to the North," he added.
Tensions have always been high along the Korean border since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce agreement, not a peace treaty.
The North formally agreed on Monday to a meeting on August 5 in New York of senior officials from the two Koreas, the United States and China to arrange four-nation peace talks.
The four-nation talks are aimed at thrashing out a permanent peace settlement to replace the fraying 1953 ceasefire pact.
